notes: §10.5.2: "**Ranges:** `a..b` excludes `b`, `a..=b` includes it (DR-24). Both are `Range[Int]`." §21.3 K0926: "`for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)`, `for i in range(n)` | `for i in 0..n:`". A Python `range(n)` loop is the §21.3 mistake whose fix is the Kalam range; it is detected in its obvious syntactic position.
